Governs U.S. arms exports. It sets the purposes for which American weapons may be sold, requires licenses for commercial sales, and gives Congress advance notice of major sales and a procedure to block them.

::: {.official-links}
**Read the law** (official GovInfo text)

[Enacted text: 90 Stat. 729](https://www.govinfo.gov/link/statute/90/729){.btn-official} [Current U.S. Code: 22 U.S.C. 2751 et seq.](https://www.govinfo.gov/link/uscode/22/2751?link-type=html){.btn-official}
:::

## Key provisions

- Secs. 3 and 4: recipients may use U.S. arms only for self-defense, internal security, and similar purposes, and may not retransfer them without consent.
- Sec. 36(b) and (c): notification to Congress of government and commercial sales above dollar thresholds, subject to a joint resolution of disapproval.
- Sec. 36 emergency provision: the President may bypass the review period by declaring an emergency.
- Sec. 38: licensing of commercial exports under the U.S. Munitions List and the International Traffic in Arms Regulations.
- Sec. 40A: end-use monitoring.

## Why it matters

Congress has never blocked a sale through a resolution of disapproval that survived a veto, so its influence runs through informal holds and conditions. The act pairs with the [Foreign Assistance Act](faa-1961.qmd) on the assistance side, with the [Export Control Reform Act](ecra-2018.qmd) for dual-use goods, and is limited by the [Leahy Laws](leahy-laws.qmd) and the [Symington-Glenn Amendments](symington-glenn.qmd).

## Current status

In force. It began as the Foreign Military Sales Act of 1968 (Pub. L. 90-629) and took its present name in 1976.

## Where it sits

- **Layer.** Framework statute. Standing laws that create institutions or general procedures other laws and executive actions plug into, such as the National Security Act, the War Powers Resolution, IEEPA, and FISA. ([How the layers work](../study/index.qmd#the-authority-stack))
- **Built upon by.** [Symington-Glenn Amendments](symington-glenn.qmd), [Taiwan Relations Act](tra-1979.qmd).
- **Codified in.** [Title 22 U.S.C.](title22-usc.qmd).
- **Era.** Vietnam, Watergate, and reassertion ([timeline](../study/timeline.qmd)).
- **Study.** [Unit 10: Arms transfers, export controls, and investment screening](../study/units/arms-transfers.qmd) (core reading); [Unit 11: Civilian harm and the conduct of operations](../study/units/civilian-harm.qmd) (further reading).
- **Member lenses.** [Rep. Jason Crow](../members/crow.qmd): Civilian Harm in Partnerships Act; Aerospace industry. [Rep. Sara Jacobs](../members/jacobs.qmd): Foreign Affairs; Security Sector Compacts Act; Stand Up for Sudan Act; Civilian Harm in Partnerships Act; Defense industry and research.
